h2: NDT training in Indiana: options across the state compared
html:
NDT training in Indiana: options across the state compared

Indiana has more heavy industry per head than almost anywhere in the country, yet a candidate searching "NDT courses near me" from Hammond, Kokomo or Evansville will not find a long list of NDT schools. Most Indiana technicians reach certification through employers and contractors, with a smaller number taking a dedicated programme in a neighbouring state. Here is how the realistic options compare.

Who offers NDT training around Indiana?

  • Ivy Tech Community College. Ivy Tech runs welding and industrial technology programmes on campuses across the state, and its Terre Haute campus has offered a short course preparing candidates for the National Board boiler and pressure vessel inspector commission examination, which touches on NDE methods. None of that is a full NDT certificate, so ask the campus near you exactly how much NDT content a programme contains and whether it documents hours per method.
  • Dedicated NDT programmes in nearby states. Community colleges in Michigan and Ohio, among other states, offer NDT certificates or courses. They suit a candidate who can commute or relocate and wants campus lab time before applying for work.
  • Mills, refiners and their contractors. The lakefront steel mills, the Whiting refinery, power stations across the south of the state and the inspection companies serving them all train and certify people. A trainee role with one of those contractors is the most common entry point, because the employer logs the experience hours that certification depends on.
  • Union apprenticeships. Indiana's building trades run apprenticeships for boilermakers, pipefitters and ironworkers. Graduates do not hold NDT certification from the apprenticeship itself, but many move into inspection roles on the same turnarounds and outages.
  • Self-paced online theory with an employer practical. This suits technicians on rotating shifts and employers who need several people qualified without sending them away.

Which route fits you?

Your situationRoute that usually fitsWhat to watch
No NDT job yetA trainee job with an inspection contractor, or a full-time programme out of stateExperience hours must be logged under an employer before you can be certified
Working technician adding UT or a second levelSelf-paced theory, then a practical on your employer's equipmentCheck your written practice accepts outside training hours
Employer qualifying a crew before an outageOn-site training at your facility with Level III oversightRefinery and utility owners may impose contractor qualification rules on top of SNT-TC-1A
Technician who travels between sitesASNT central certification alongside employer certificationASNT sets and administers the examinations

Questions to ask any NDT training provider in Indiana

  1. How many training hours does the course document per method and level?
  2. Will my employer's written practice accept those hours, and will the provider put that in writing?
  3. Who runs the practical, and on what: welds, plate, castings, tubes, forgings?
  4. Who certifies me at the end? Under SNT-TC-1A the answer is always the employer.
  5. Is a Level III available for questions during the course?
  6. Does the course help with ASNT central certification if I want it later?

One Indiana detail matters for anyone choosing a radiography course. Indiana became an NRC Agreement State at the end of September 2026, so industrial radiography licensing now runs through the state's own radioactive materials program rather than the NRC. An RT theory course still licenses nobody: the radiography company holds the licence and qualifies the people who handle sources.

Where Atlantis fits for Indiana candidates and employers

Atlantis NDT has no classroom in Indiana. Theory is self-paced on the Atlantis portal with question-and-answer support from an ASNT NDT Level III, and access opens as soon as you enrol. Practicals run in the Practical NDT simulator and then in person on real parts at the employer's mill, plant or shop, under a written practice built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A. For a lakefront contractor that means training a crew on its own UT and MT equipment ahead of a turnaround, without losing people to weeks away.

Course pages: UT training, MT training, NDT Level 2 training and ASNT Level III preparation. Local detail is on the Indianapolis, Fort Wayne and Evansville pages, and welding inspectors can look at CWI exam prep for Indianapolis.
